feature: Marketing Buy / Checkout page (/buy) — the one checkout for all three products. Asserts the product-specific rules that make or break the flow: monitoring gates pricing+payment behind a tenant connection, retainer offers a skippable scan and is never gated, packs are multi-select with a summed one-time total, and the terms checkbox gates the pay button without ever hiding the payment fields.

SCOPE — the deterministic, no-timer assertions that prove each product's own checkout rule:
MONITORING (gated): /buy?product=monitoring&seats=250 renders the 'Connect first' heading, the
read-only connect card, and a pay button reading 'Connect your tenant to continue'; the payment
fields are ABSENT until the tenant is connected (README: monitoring cannot be priced before the
tenant reports its seat count).
MONITORING (from a scan): /buy?product=monitoring&scanned=1 skips the connect step, shows the
connected card and the payment fields, prices on the real 1,240-seat tenant figure (Growth tier
= $9,920/mo), and the terms box gates the pay button ('Accept the terms to continue' -> 'Pay
$9,920 and start' once ticked) WITHOUT hiding the payment fields.
RETAINER (skippable, never gated): /buy?product=retainer&tier=essentials shows 'Pick your hours',
an optional Skip button, the payment fields (no connect gate), a $1,500/mo total, and the same
terms gate ('Pay $1,500 and start').
PACK (multi-select, summed): /buy?product=pack&packs=entra,ca sums to $998 (no /mo), reads '2
packs, one dry run', shows the payment fields, and gates on terms ('Pay $998 and continue').
PACK (not-yet-available gating, Git #1304, repointed at 'copilot' by #4321): /buy?product=pack&packs=entra,copilot
-- useQuickStartPackAvailability() cross-references PACKS against the real live `services`
table by name (no real row for Copilot Readiness today, per a direct query against local
Postgres run for #4321 -- MFA Enforcement, the pack this test originally targeted, now HAS a
real services row and had to be repointed); its option row renders a 'Coming soon' badge and
is dropped from the URL-preselected packSel once the live read resolves, leaving only Entra ID
Quick-Start selected ($799, not $1,298). This is the same gate /quick-start's own catalogue
uses, so a pack can never be paid for silently just because it lacks real backend fulfillment.
Only as stable as the live catalogue's current state -- if Copilot Readiness is later onboarded
as a real services row, repoint at whatever is genuinely not-yet-real then. This is also the
first live network call this otherwise-fixture-driven page makes; the 'NO backend' note below
now applies to every OTHER assertion in this manifest.
GIT #1317 (sessionTag 1317-integration): the post-payment flow is no longer simulated — every
stage transition is a real endpoint call (read consent popup+poll #1311, write consent #1312,
Stripe #1307/#1308, code/password/MFA #1310, monitoring scan kickoff riding set-password #1314,
portal auto-login handoff #1313/#1315, pack dry-run/execute #1316). Consequences asserted here:
contact fields render pre-connect for every product (the consent URL is minted against a session
created from them), ?scanned=1 no longer fabricates a connection or a fake 1,240-seat price, and
packs surface the REQUIRED read-consent connect card before payment. The paid happy path (real
Microsoft consent, real Stripe charge, real emailed code, real TOTP enrollment, real portal
auto-login, real pack dry-run/execute) cannot run from fixture-free manifest steps — it was
exercised in the #1317 session via a full Playwright UI E2E per product against this exact code
(see artifacts/api-server/_tmp_1317_e2e.mjs): Monitoring 19/19, Retainer 16/16, Pack 23/23, with
the pack execute reaching a REAL Graph write refused 403 by the write app's missing directory
permission (Azure-side, Shane To-Do on #1317).
DEPLOYED-ORIGIN CAVEAT (same class the sibling marketing manifests carry): this asserts against
{{DEPLOY_URL}}, which only reflects the new marketing site — and this page — once that site is
redeployed. Until the Part 0+ rebuild is the deployed frontend, /buy resolves to the old site's 404
fallback and these steps fail on that ground alone, not on a page defect. lastVerifiedAgainstCommit
is PENDING for that reason; the code itself is verified green locally as noted above.
